target_in_paper: Question 15.4 in Section 15 (equation (15.5)), immediately following Conjecture 15.3 in the section "Arithmetic Degrees of Orbits."
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly keeps the ambient space as projective space \(\mathbf{P}^N\), takes \(f\) to be a dominant rational self-map defined over \(\overline{\mathbf{Q}}\), assumes the chosen point has Zariski-dense forward orbit, asks for the precise growth shape \(\delta_f^n n^{\ell_f}(\log n)^{k_f}\), includes the bound \(0\le \ell_f\le N\), and includes the paper’s follow-up question asking whether \(k_f=0\) when \(\delta_f>1\). Your added contextual remarks about the morphism case and Sano’s result also match the nearby text of the paper.
missing_details: The exact target in the paper is Question 15.4, not Example 15.5; equation (15.5) is the displayed formula inside Question 15.4.
The notation \(h\) should be defined as the projective logarithmic height on \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})\), introduced in Definition 15.1.
The notation \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\) must be defined: it is the set of points whose entire forward orbit under \(f\) is well-defined (Definition 15.2).
The orbit notation \(O_f(P)\) should be explicitly defined as \(\{f^n(P): n\ge 0\}\).
The notation \(\delta_f\) should be defined as the dynamical degree \(\delta_f=\lim_{n\to\infty}(\deg(f^n))^{1/n}\) from Definition 14.2.

The symbol \(\asymp\) (or \(\approx\)/\(\≍\) in the paper) should be unpacked: there exist positive constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3\) such that the two-sided inequality holds for all \(n\ge c_3\) (footnote 23).

To be fully stand-alone, the question should state that the constants in the two-sided estimate depend on \(f\) and \(P\), but not on \(n\), and that the estimate is meant for all sufficiently large \(n\).
The official wording only constrains \(\ell_f\) by \(0\le \ell_f\le N\); it does not separately impose \(k_f\ge 0\).
The nearby paper context ties this question to Conjecture 15.3(d), which predicts \(\alpha_f(P)=\delta_f\) for Zariski-dense orbit; your draft does not make that motivation explicit.

The paper says this is the arithmetic analogue of Question 14.16; that connection helps delimit the intended scope and should be noted in the justification, though it need not appear inside the final question itself.
The contextual morphism statement belongs to Section 16 via the canonical height \(\hat h_f\); it is supporting context, not part of the core question itself.
The paper’s core question is specifically on \(\mathbf{P}^N\); remarks about general varieties are supplementary and should not replace or broaden the main target.
refined_question: Let \(f:\mathbf{P}^N\dashrightarrow \mathbf{P}^N\) be a dominant rational map defined over \(\overline{\mathbf{Q}}\), let \(\delta_f:=\lim_{n\to\infty}(\deg(f^n))^{1/n}\) be its dynamical degree, let \(h\) be the logarithmic Weil height on \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})\), and let \(P\in \mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\), where \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\) denotes the set of points whose entire forward orbit \(O_f(P)=\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\}\) is well-defined. Assume that \(O_f(P)\) is Zariski dense in \(\mathbf{P}^N\). Must there exist integers \(k_f\) and \(\ell_f\), with \(0\le \ell_f\le N\), such that there are constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3>0\), depending on \(f\) and \(P\), for which \(c_1\,\delta_f^n n^{\ell_f}(\log n)^{k_f}\le h(f^n(P))\le c_2\,\delta_f^n n^{\ell_f}(\log n)^{k_f}\) for all \(n\ge c_3\)? Moreover, if \(\delta_f>1\), must one have \(k_f=0\)?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s official open problem on refined height growth in projective space, namely Question 15.4. This is clear because the draft reproduces the displayed formula (15.5), the Zariski-dense-orbit hypothesis, and the follow-up question about whether the logarithmic exponent vanishes when \(\delta_f>1\). The nearby context shows that this question is posed right after Conjecture 15.3(d), which predicts \(\alpha_f(P)=\delta_f\) for Zariski-dense orbits, and the paper explicitly says Question 15.4 is an arithmetic analogue of Question 14.16. To make the problem fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the definitions of height, arithmetic orbit domain \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\), dynamical degree, and the exact meaning of \(\asymp\). The morphism remark belongs to Section 16 and supports, but does not alter, the scope of the question.
